emulation.notes: Use a legal DS dump. High-resolution 3D rendering through GPU scaling is available via DeSmuME, but this game still depends on DS-native 2D/touch presentation, so prioritize accurate layout, text readability, and stylus response over aggressive filtering.

primary.version: European Nintendo DS release via DS emulation
primary.why: Freshly-Picked Tingle's Rosy Rupeeland released on Nintendo DS, with stylus input and one-player support. Japan was the 2006 launch region and Europe received the later official English release, with no North American release. Because no remaster, port, or higher-fidelity platform exists, the European DS release in a modern DS emulator is the best complete route for an English playthrough.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped European Nintendo DS cartridge in melonDS or DeSmuME. Preserve both DS screens and touch/stylus input; use clean integer or high-quality scaling and a side-by-side or vertical layout that keeps map, touch prompts, and combat visible. Use the Japanese original only for language/version comparison.

all_releases.fidelity: Only sourced platform; best archive fidelity comes from a clean DS dump in modern DS emulation with carefully captured dual screens and touch input.
all_releases.reason: primary: Nintendo DS is the release platform, with a Japan 2006 release and Europe 2007 release. The European DS version is the practical English complete route and no separate remaster or exclusive-content platform exists.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced alternate platform, remaster, or exclusive-content release exists. The only practical choice is region/language: the European DS release provides official English text, while the Japanese original is the first release.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster, Switch/3DS/Wii U port, PC version, or North American release is sourced. DS capture needs thoughtful dual-screen layout because the game uses stylus and touch-screen interactions.
